• ArchitecturalDecision — "query() adds PureSymbolic fallback when SchemaQuerySpec internal error leaks into answer; query_with_llm_client seam enables LLM injection in tests"
  hasDescription: Commit 69f8f01389 (src/graph/mod.rs, tests/query.rs). `query()` is refactored into three layers: private `execute_query()` takes explicit `llm` + `engine_config` refs; public `query()` calls `execute_query` with the state's own llm/model/engine_config; `#[doc(hidden)]` pub `query_with_llm_client()` accepts an injected `&dyn LlmClient` for test determinism. The fallback logic lives in `query_with_llm_client`: if the assist level is not PureSymbolic and the returned answer contains the internal sentinel string `SCHEMA_QUERY_SPEC_INTERNAL_ERROR` ("Schema query intent set but no SchemaQuerySpec was attached"), the pipeline retries with `llm_assist_level = LlmAssistLevel::PureSymbolic` on a cloned config. Rationale: `execute_graph_walk_nlq_with_context` can emit that sentinel as a diagnostic when a schema-query intent is resolved but no SchemaQuerySpec is attached, and without the fallback that internal error leaks verbatim to the MCP caller. The regression test `query_does_not_surface_schema_spec_internal_error_for_project_records` uses `MetaIntentLlm` (a stub that returns a meta-intent JSON response) to trigger the code path and assert that (a) the error string never reaches the answer, and (b) the trace confirms PureSymbolic was used on the retry.

  hasDescription: Commit 64f9fbf1b7 ("simplify pass, plus most of M1") introduces src/lib.rs, making moosedev a combined library+binary crate. All substantive modules (graph, llm, mcp, ontology) live in the lib crate; src/main.rs remains a thin wrapper that serves MooseDevServer over stdio. Rationale: every module is reachable from integration tests in tests/ — the lib boundary is the test seam. Previously the project was binary-only, which would have made integration testing impossible without re-exposing internals.

  linkedVia: constrains
  hasDescription: MOOSEDev is designed as a neurosymbolic MCP server whose core purpose is to combat comprehension debt — the gradual loss of understanding of why a codebase is structured the way it is. It serves as an early example of a domain-specific, epistemically grounded AI application. Built on top of the closed-source MOOSE neurosymbolic engine; MOOSEDev itself is open source. Rationale: push back against LLMs that optimize for sounding correct rather than being correct, by emphasizing symbolic reasoning, structured typed knowledge, auditability, and a living project knowledge graph. item.text: I found the implementation in the MOOSEDev source tree; next I’ll read the actual `get_relevant_context` handler and summarize the live mechanism from that code path.

`get_relevant_context` calls `graph::relevant_context`. When a `topic` is provided, it performs **symbolic BM25 lexical retrieval** via `entity_index.search_records` over each record’s `rurtle:` title (`rdfs:label`) and description (weights 2.0 and 1.0), over `InformationRecord` subclasses in the project KG, then returns the top-k hits and builds context items.  

After that, it filters out `superseded/deprecated` items by default unless `include_history=true`, and for topic queries it may additionally expand to a small bounded set of linked neighbors (up to configured hops) from the top-ranked seeds to improve completeness without dumping full graph neighborhoods.
